newsitem.title: INDONESIA: U.N. envoy urges continued E.Timor dialogue.
newsitem.headline: U.N. envoy urges continued E.Timor dialogue.

text.p: The United Nations special envoy on East Timor said on Thursday a productive dialogue was needed to achieve an acceptable international solution over the former Portuguese colony annexed by Indonesia two decades ago.

"The important thing is that the dialogue should continue...and we have to find means of ensuring not only that the dialogue continues, but it is productive," envoy Jamsheed Marker told reporters after meeting President Suharto.

Marker, appointed by Secretary-General Kofi Annan last month as his special assistant for East Timor, arrived in Jakarta on Thursday on what the U.N. described as a "familiarisation" visit. He was due to visit East Timor over the weekend.
"The United Nations is at the disposal...of all the parties for any assistance that can be given on the subject of East Timor," he said.
"I informed (Suharto) that I am here on a fact-finding mission basically and I will report back to the secretary-general," he added.
Indonesia invaded East Timor in December 1975 with tacit Western support after civil war broke out there following the departure of Portuguese colonial authorities.
Indonesia incorporated East Timor as its 27th province the following July in a move not recognised by the United Nations.

Marker, a former Pakistani ambassador to the United Nations, said the world body would hold further discussions on steps to be taken over East Timor after his visit to Indonesia. He did not elaborate.
U.N.-sponsored talks between Indonesia and Portugal over East Timor's future have been underway for nearly 15 years without an agreement.
Marker visited Portugal earlier this month and said in Lisbon he hoped for a speed-up in the talks.

Foreign Minister Ali Alatas, who accompanied Marker to his meeting with Suharto, said the president welcomed the envoy's visit and hoped he could find an objective perspective after visiting the territory.
"It is hoped that after the visit he can collect an objective perception on the real situation which can help solve the problem of East Timor completely and fairly," Alatas said.
Meanwhile, a senior U.S. human rights official flew to the East Timorese capital of Dili on Thursday for a two-day fact-finding visit.
John Shattuck, assistant secretary of state for democracy, human rights and labour, is spending two days in East Timor before leaving for Cambodia on Friday night.
